turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the programme is crawling again. Mrs Naidoo? Have a seat while I get this screen to behave.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. Priya Naidoo. Thank you for fitting me in at short notice.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, no trouble at all. What brings you in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The burning has come back when I pass urine. It is quite unpleasant, I am afraid.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Burning when you pass urine. How long has this particular bout gone on?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Thursday, so four days. It stings most at the very end.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Has this happened before, or is it the first time?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It is the third time this year, Doctor.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I ought to correct that. It may be the fourth. There was a short spell in February I had put out of my mind.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that once more? The screen just refreshed itself.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): February, then May, then July, and now this one. So perhaps the fourth time this year.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Any fever with it?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I have been going to the toilet far more often, twice during the night as well, which is difficult with work.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): I was asking about fever. Any temperature, or chills?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. No fever and no chills. I apologise, I answered a different question.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the urine?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood that I have noticed.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain in the back or over the loin, or is it only low down?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Only low down, Doctor. There is no back pain.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): And any vaginal discharge, or itching?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing of that sort. I would really rather not—
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): We can leave it. Are you taking any medicines just now?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I am embarrassed to say, Doctor. It is not something I am proud of.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): I would rather you told me. Please go ahead.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I took leftover antibiotic tablets that belonged to my sister. I know I should not have.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you mean the nursing sister, or your own sister?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): My sibling, Doctor. She lives in Durban. The tablets were in her wash bag from a visit.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I started them because the burning was so—
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hold on, a box has popped up. You did swallow some. Which antibiotic, slowly?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): The bottle said ciprofloxacin. I think the dose was five hundred milligrams.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): How often did you take it, and for how many days? Say it again, I have typed in the wrong place.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): By mouth, twice a day, for three days. I stopped on Sunday, as it was not helping the burning.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stopped on Sunday. Did you take any other tablets of hers?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): There was biotin in the same bag, for her hair. I did not touch the biotin. Only the antibiotic.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Her biotin, not yours. I will not add it. Do you take any medicine of your own every day?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): None of my own. My husband did press one of his metformin tablets on me. He has diabetes, and he had been reading nonsense. I declined.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Quite right, do not take his metformin. Sorry, I was clearing a reminder. So no daily tablets of your own?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): None at all, Doctor.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I am aware of.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I must ask again about the vaginal symptoms, because ciprofloxacin can set itching off. Is there any discharge or itch?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I did say no. Well, actually, there has been a little itching for two days, and perhaps a slight white discharge. I was too embarrassed the first time.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Itching for two days. When did the discharge begin?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I cannot date it, Doctor. It may only be since yesterday, and I may be imagining it.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pain during intercourse?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): We have not been intimate this week, so I really cannot say if—
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we will leave that. Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhoea?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): No nausea, no vomiting, and no diarrhoea.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): And you are not diabetic yourself.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not. He is the one with diabetes. Dis-Chem checked my sugar last year and said it was normal.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or take alcohol?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I have one glass of wine on a Friday evening. I work as a bookkeeper in Rosebank, mostly at a desk.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): May I examine your abdomen?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly, Doctor.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): The abdomen is soft. There is mild tenderness just above the pubic bone. No tenderness in either loin.

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Triage figures, if this window will stay open: temperature thirty-six point eight, heart rate seventy-six, blood pressure one twenty-eight over seventy-eight, oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent.

[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am thinking aloud, and I am not going to conclude that this is definitely another urine infection. It could be cystitis again, it could be the ciprofloxacin irritating the bladder, and the itch could be thrush from the antibiotic. Let's see what the urine says before I put a name to it.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand, Doctor. I will not take her tablets again. I feel rather foolish.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): It is unsafe, and it muddies the culture, so I am glad you will stop that. How much water are you drinking in a day?
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister telephones every Sunday to scold me about water, and then my mother comes on the line, and I simply—
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Forgive me, I wandered. About a litre a day, I should think.
[SEG0062] person_1 (DOCTOR): That is on the low side. Drink more, steadily, through the day. I am sending a midstream urine for dipstick, microscopy and culture just now.
[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): Will you be prescribing an antibiotic today?
[SEG0064] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. We may chase the wrong germ if we guess. Paracetamol one gram, up to four times a day, if the burning is troublesome and it suits you.

[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back if it is not settling in three days, or sooner should you develop fever, vomiting, or pain in the loin. Reception will telephone when the culture is back, usually within two or three days.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): I have paracetamol at home already. Thank you for explaining it so carefully.
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): You are welcome, Mrs Naidoo. Please leave the sample at the desk on your way out.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall. Good afternoon, Doctor.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Husband having diabetes is stated, but this is not family history.
Burning, unpleasant, since Thursday/four days, fourth this year supported; body_site urethra not stated.

omissions.text: Dysuria stings most at the very end of urination.
Current fluid intake is about 1 litre per day, noted as low by the doctor.
Ciprofloxacin was stopped on Sunday because it was not helping the burning.

Negative finding asked and answered: no vaginal discharge or itching was initially denied, then corrected; final history is that there has been a little itching for 2 days and perhaps slight white discharge since yesterday.
Question about pain during intercourse was not answered because the patient said they had not been intimate this week, so she could not say.
Doctor explicitly said he was not concluding this was definitely another urine infection before seeing the urine results.
